exercises.title: Adding in memory
exercises.statement: The starting code writes two unsigned words to memory, at `$2000` (`$1234`) and `$2002` (`$0111`). Add them and put the result in D0 (and at address `$2004`).
hints: First read the two values back from memory with MOVE.W before adding them.
ADD.W <ea>,D0 adds the source to the destination register.

exercises.title: Unsigned multiplication
exercises.statement: Compute the unsigned product of 9 and 6 using MULU, with the result in D2.
hints: MULU.W <ea>,Dn puts the full product in the 32 bits of Dn, so there is no separate overflow to handle.
First put one of the two values in D2, then multiply by the other (immediate).

exercises.title: A chain of logical operations
exercises.statement: Put `$F0F0` in D0, then apply in order: a logical AND with `$0FF0`, a logical OR with `$000F`, then an EXCLUSIVE OR with `$FFFF`, each operation changing D0.
hints: AND.W, OR.W and EOR.W work like MOVE.W: <source>,<destination>.
Work it out bit by bit on paper to check each step: $F0F0, then $00F0, then $00FF, then $FF00.

exercises.title: ASL and LSR shifts
exercises.statement: Put `3` in D0 (word), shift it left by 4 bits with ASL, then right by 1 bit with LSR.
hints: ASL.W #n,Dn shifts left while preserving the sign; LSR.W #n,Dn shifts right, bringing in zeros.
3 shifted left by 4 gives 48 ($30); 48 shifted right by 1 gives 24 ($18).

exercises.title: NEG and NOT
exercises.statement: Put `5` (long) in D0, then apply NEG.L (two's complement) and NOT.L (one's complement) to D0.
hints: NOT.L Dn flips every bit of Dn.
NEG of 5 gives -5 ($FFFFFFFB); NOT of $FFFFFFFB gives $00000004.
